page_title: Building a simple Chat app with Elixir and Phoenix

sources.entry: Building a Simple Chat App With Elixir and Phoenix

summary.title: Building a simple Chat app with Elixir and Phoenix
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a minimal real-time chat app in Elixir using Phoenix channels and websockets, with no authentication.
keywords: how to build chat with phoenix
takeaways: Create a Phoenix project and set up a simple markup and CSS view for a chat window.
Define a Phoenix channel called lobby with join and handle_in functions that broadcast messages to all open sockets.
Register the channel in user_socket.ex and connect it on the client with Phoenix's built-in socket.js.
Push messages from a text field on keypress and append incoming messages to the page with jQuery.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a basic chat application with the Phoenix Framework for Elixir, skipping authentication and authorization. It creates a new Phoenix project, adds a template with a message list and input fields, and styles the list with CSS. It then defines a "lobby" channel whose handle_in function broadcasts each incoming message to all connected sockets. Finally, it wires up the client in socket.js using jQuery to push messages on Enter and append received messages to the page.
